title: First Day at Work
author: Barashada Ingiriisiga
description: Yusuf starts his first job at a supermarket and learns to greet customers, stock shelves, and ask for help, discovering that small steps build confidence at work.

chapters.title: First Day at the Market
chapters.text:
Yusuf stood outside the big supermarket and looked at the door. It was seven o'clock in the morning, and the sun was just coming up. He was early for his first day at work. His hands were a little cold, and his heart was beating fast. He took a deep breath and pushed the door open.

Inside, the lights were bright. A woman in a blue uniform walked towards him and smiled. "You must be Yusuf. I am Mrs. Ali, the manager. Welcome."

"Thank you," Yusuf said. His voice was quiet.

"Come with me," Mrs. Ali said. "I will show you around."

They walked down the first aisle. There were boxes of cereal, bags of rice, and jars of jam. Yusuf looked at everything. There was so much to remember.

"This is Aisle One," Mrs. Ali said. "Here we have breakfast food. Aisle Two has drinks. Aisle Three has bread and cakes. And over there, we have fruit and vegetables."

Yusuf nodded. He tried to remember the names. Breakfast, drinks, bread, fruit. It was a lot of new information.

"Don't worry," Mrs. Ali said. "You will learn quickly. Now, let me teach you something important. When a customer comes near you, you say, 'Hello, welcome.' Can you try?"

Yusuf looked at his feet. He felt nervous. "Hello... welcome," he said softly.

"Good," Mrs. Ali said. "But speak a little louder. The customers need to hear you. Try again."

Yusuf took a breath. "Hello, welcome!" he said, louder this time.

"Very good," Mrs. Ali said. "Now, let me show you how to stock the shelves. We put the new products at the back and the old products at the front. Do you understand?"

Yusuf was not sure. He wanted to ask, but he felt shy. He looked at the shelf and thought about it. Then he said, "Excuse me, Mrs. Ali. Can you show me again, please?"

Mrs. Ali smiled. "Of course, Yusuf. Watch me."

She took a box of cereal from a big cart. She put the old box at the front and the new box behind it. "See? Old at the front, new at the back. Now you try."

Yusuf picked up a box. He put the old one at the front and the new one at the back. He did it again and again. Soon, the shelf was full.

"Excellent work," Mrs. Ali said.

Just then, the door opened. A customer came in. Yusuf felt his heart beat again. He looked at the woman and said, "Hello, welcome!"

The customer smiled at him. "Good morning," she said.

Yusuf smiled too. It was not so hard. He was ready for his first day.

chapters.title: Learning the Shelves
chapters.text:
The next morning, Yusuf arrived at the supermarket at eight o'clock. Mrs. Ali was waiting for him near the storeroom. She smiled and said, "Today you will learn the shelves. We have many products, and every product has a place. When a shelf is empty, we fill it again. This is called stocking."

Mrs. Ali gave Yusuf a small machine. It was a price checker. She showed him how to use it. "You point this at the label on a product, and it shows the price. Customers often ask about prices. You can check for them."

Yusuf nodded. He was nervous but ready to learn.

Mrs. Ali took him to the canned goods aisle. There were many cans on the shelves. Beans, tomatoes, soup, and corn. She showed him the labels. "Each can has a small number on the back. This number tells us the price. We put the cans in rows. The labels must face the front. That looks nice for customers."

Yusuf started to work. He picked up cans and placed them on the shelves. He worked slowly but carefully. After some time, he saw a box of cans on the floor. The label said "red beans." Yusuf looked at the shelf. He saw red beans and put the new cans there. He felt happy. He was doing well.

But then a customer came to him. She held a can and asked, "How much is this?" Yusuf took his price checker and pointed it at the label. The machine showed a price. Yusuf told the customer, "It is two dollars." The customer looked at the can and said, "But the label here says one dollar." Yusuf looked again. He saw that the shelf had the wrong cans. He had put the red beans in the wrong place. The shelf was for white beans.

Yusuf felt his face get hot. He was embarrassed. He did not know what to do. He thought about the cans he had placed. Many of them were wrong.

He looked for Mrs. Ali. He found her in the next aisle. He said, "Mrs. Ali, I made a mistake. I put the red beans in the wrong place. I am sorry."

Mrs. Ali did not look angry. She smiled and said, "Good. You asked for help. That is the rule here. If you don't know, ask. Never guess. Guessing can make problems. Asking is always better."

She showed him how to read the labels more carefully. Together, they moved the cans to the right shelves. Yusuf watched and learned. When they finished, Mrs. Ali said, "Now you know. Well done."

Yusuf felt much better. He was not a bad worker. He just needed to ask. He smiled and said, "Thank you, Mrs. Ali. I will ask next time."

chapters.title: A Small Success
chapters.text:
Yusuf arrived at the supermarket for his second day. He felt better than yesterday. He knew the way to the staff room. He knew where to put his bag. He put on his blue uniform and smiled at himself in the mirror.

Mrs. Ali was waiting for him near the fruit. "Good morning, Yusuf," she said. "Today, you will help customers. You will also stock the tea shelves. Do you remember the greeting?"

"Yes, Mrs. Ali," Yusuf said. "Hello, welcome."

"Very good," she said. "Let's begin."

Yusuf walked to the tea section. There were many boxes of tea. Green tea, black tea, and herbal tea. He started to put new boxes on the shelves. He worked slowly and carefully. He checked the prices on the boxes. He made sure the labels faced the front.

After an hour, an old woman came to the tea section. She looked at the shelves. She looked at the boxes. She did not look happy.

Yusuf remembered his greeting. "Hello, welcome," he said. He tried to smile, but his smile was small.

The woman looked at him. "I need some tea," she said. "But I do not know which one to buy. I want something for my stomach. It hurts."

Yusuf did not know about tea for stomachs. He felt nervous. He wanted to help, but he did not know the answer. Then he remembered what Mrs. Ali said. "If you don't know, ask."

"One moment, please," he said to the woman. He walked to find Mrs. Ali. She was near the bread.

"Excuse me, Mrs. Ali," he said. "A customer needs tea for her stomach. I do not know which tea is good for that."

Mrs. Ali smiled. "Good question, Yusuf. That is the peppermint tea. It is on the top shelf. I will show you."

She walked with Yusuf to the tea section. She pointed to a green box. "This is peppermint tea," she said. "It is good for stomachs."

Yusuf took the box. He walked to the woman. "This is peppermint tea," he said. "It is good for your stomach."

The woman took the box and looked at it. She smiled. "Thank you," she said. "You are very helpful."

Yusuf felt warm inside. His smile was big now. "You're welcome," he said. "Have a nice day."

The woman walked to the checkout. Yusuf watched her go. He felt proud.

Later, Mrs. Ali came to him. "Yusuf, I saw you help that customer," she said. "You asked for help. That is very good. You did a small thing, but it was a big help for her. You did a good job today."

"Thank you, Mrs. Ali," Yusuf said.

At five o'clock, his shift ended. He took off his uniform and walked out of the store. The sun was warm on his face. He thought about the old woman and her smile. He thought about Mrs. Ali's words.

He walked home slowly. He felt happy. He had a small success today. And he was ready for his next day.
